description: The peoples canon recognises, declared once so that a culture is a value rather than a typo waiting to happen. The companion to clades.json and growth_forms.json: those say what an animal and a plant are, this says what a person belongs to.
note: `asura` is deliberately absent. It had been doing three jobs at once -- a culture on characters, a species on characters, and a prefix on thirty-one creatures -- and the three are different things. The culture is `maya_born`, the maya-born humanoids who are people rather than beasts. The species sense stays on `species`. And an asura creature is its own species paired with a base animal: a wolf and an asura wolf are two species, not one animal with a flag.

cultures.dress: Cotton, worn wrapped and draped, and dyed -- madder red, indigo, turmeric, ochre -- as often as it is left the colour of the boll. Harappan settlers wear their wealth where it can be seen, when they have any: a little gold or silver at the ear, the wrist or the nose, and beads of lapis lazuli, carnelian and other stones brought a long way. The families take wives from beyond their own realm, so a Harappan household is often of more than one people to look at, and nobody there thinks it worth remarking on.
cultures.art_reference: Reference only, for whoever paints them; not a claim about any people living today. Faces and builds after the peoples of Gujarat, Sindh and Punjab. Some women, married in from beyond the realm, after the peoples of Bengal and Odisha.

cultures.note:
The one culture here that is not a people. Every other entry names a lineage you are born into; this one names a way of moving through the world, and it is why the same word fits a Tushara nomad girl, a Civilization Dawn whale-blimp commander and a god wearing a mortal frame.

Six hold it, across four eras and every kind of vessel canon has: Varuna captains the Kelpfang and Mitra navigates it; Rathak runs cargo over the Tethys by airship; Ruvan walks, and is the observer the others are measured against; Guyuk crosses the steppe on foot and her second life crosses the ruined grasslands by train. What they share is not ancestry or territory but a disposition -- they go and look, and they bring back an account.

That is also the player's disposition, which is not an accident. The game is one long field journey and Varuna is the character you are; the culture is the one canon offers as an answer to what kind of person does that.

cultures.dress: The delta's own people, and they dress like it: light wrapped cloth dyed in the marsh's colours, and flowers -- worn in the hair, behind the ear, strung as a garland. Hair is dressed with care and at length, coiled, braided and pinned with shell and bone, by men and women both. Their women are full-figured, and nobody among the Kia would think that needed saying.
cultures.art_reference: Reference only, for whoever paints them; not a claim about any people living today. Faces and builds after the peoples of Maharashtra, the Konkan coast and Kerala; some after Austronesian peoples, as far as the Philippines.

cultures.note: Asura-blooded people. Before the Cataclysm, the Asura-Tainted Princess alone. After it, Narakalok fractured and half-breeds began to mingle with humans in the north and west -- Bahlika, Kush, Hyrkania -- and, as Asia grew less hospitable, to worship the old asuras and wake them. The hybrid nomads are her people. Not yet met on the road in the field diary: its strangers are drawn from harappan, kia and maru only, and the owner has the asura hybrids walk as Maru for now.
Named in the prose of the Lothal guilds. Nobody currently holds it: Rathak, its only bearer, is an explorer who trades rather than a trader who travels.

The steppe people Guyuk was born to. She now carries `explorer`, which is a disposition rather than a birth, so nobody in canon currently holds this. The people are named across the prose and the declaration stays.

The plateau herders, named for the language canon already gives them -- `maru` is the tongue Marn speaks and the vocabulary folder carries its words. Declared as a culture because a recipe needed to say whose knowledge it is: setting curd from a browsing animal is theirs, and 'harappan' would have been a lie about a people three hundred miles downriver.

Count zero because culture sits on characters and canon's characters are elsewhere; the people are named through their language, their terraces and their herder.
cultures.dress: Newer to these roads than the delta's peoples, and nomads still: they dress for the upland and the cold night rather than the marsh. Animal fur and skin -- goat, sheep, whatever the herd gave -- worn as vests, cloaks and collars over wool and felt, with dyed cloth where they have traded for it.
cultures.art_reference: Reference only, for whoever paints them; not a claim about any people living today. Faces and builds after the peoples of Himachal and Nepal; some after Tibetan peoples. Not everybody among them should look East Asian.

given_names_note: Given names a people uses, for the people the game meets without canon having written them -- the carriers, drovers and pilgrims on the road. Declared on the culture so a name is a value of a people rather than an invention of the engine: the game deals them, canon owns them. Only the three peoples alive on the field maps in epoch_post_cataclysm carry a list. Names are ungendered, as canon's own people's names are; nothing here decides who a stranger is beyond what they are called. Each list was written in its people's sound -- Harappan codas in -ek, -ik, -en, -ar and doubled vowels (Kavik, Orek, Aasha); Kia short with -kh, -sh or an open vowel (Bekh, Hesh, Thrali); Maru nasal and rounded (Moonj, Marn, Okhi) -- and checked against every person, place and word in canon so none is somebody who already exists. The lint refuses a given name that is.
dress_note: `dress` is canon: how a people clothes and adorns itself, which the game's art follows. `art_reference` is not canon about the world -- it names real-world peoples as a painter's reference for faces and builds, and nothing in the world of this game is those peoples. Only the three peoples alive on the field maps in epoch_post_cataclysm carry either, because only they are painted. Added at the owner's direction, 2026-09-25.
